_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Canada covering First Peoples (Beringia migration, First Nations, Inuit, Métis), Norse Vinland ~1000 CE, Cabot/Cartier/Champlain, New France, fur trade (Hudson's Bay Company), Seven Years' War/Plains of Abraham 1759, British North America, Confederation 1867, Riel Rebellions, residential schools (cultural genocide), both World Wars (Vimy Ridge), Quebec separatism, multiculturalism, Charter of Rights 1982, and Truth & Reconciliation.

religion.note: Rapidly secularizing; Catholic historically dominant (Quebec, French-Canadian identity); United Church uniquely Canadian; growing Muslim/Hindu/Sikh (immigration); Indigenous spirituality; residential school trauma legacy

ethnic_groups.name: European descent
ethnic_groups.notes: British (English, Scottish, Irish) and French (Québécois); also German, Ukrainian (prairies), Dutch, Italian, Polish; 'two founding nations' narrative (English/French); Atlantic Canada Celtic roots

ethnic_groups.name: Indigenous (First Nations, Métis, Inuit)
ethnic_groups.notes: ~1.8M; First Nations (634 bands, treaties); Métis (mixed French-Indigenous, Red River); Inuit (Arctic, Nunavut created 1999); residential schools (1831-1996, ~150,000 children, cultural genocide, mass graves); MMIWG crisis; Truth and Reconciliation 2015; overincarceration

ethnic_groups.name: South Asian
ethnic_groups.notes: Punjabi Sikhs (Punjab to BC since 1897, Komagata Maru 1914); Indian, Pakistani, Sri Lankan; Brampton ('Bramladesh'); largest visible minority group

ethnic_groups.name: Chinese
ethnic_groups.notes: Longest-standing Asian community; Gold Rush/CPR railroad (deadly conditions, head tax 1885-1923, exclusion); Vancouver/Toronto; Cantonese and Mandarin

ethnic_groups.name: Black/African descent
ethnic_groups.notes: Historic Black communities (Nova Scotia since 1780s, Loyalists, Underground Railroad); Caribbean immigration (Jamaican, Trinidadian); African immigration growing; Africville demolition

ethnic_groups.name: Filipino
ethnic_groups.notes: Labour migration; care workers; Manitoba significant population

ethnic_groups.name: Arab
ethnic_groups.notes: Lebanese, Syrian, Iraqi; Montreal significant community

ethnic_groups.name: Other visible minorities
ethnic_groups.notes: Korean, Japanese, Southeast Asian, West Asian; multicultural mosaic policy since 1971

independence.from: United Kingdom (gradual process, not a single date)

country_profile.notes_unique: Second-largest country by area (world); bilingual English/French; 'mosaic' multiculturalism (vs US 'melting pot'); universal healthcare (Tommy Douglas, 'Greatest Canadian'); residential schools (cultural genocide, Truth and Reconciliation); Vimy Ridge 1917 (national identity); Quebec separatism (1980/1995 referendums, 1995 lost by 1%); maple leaf/hockey/Tim Hortons; RCMP; oil sands (Alberta); peacekeeping tradition; Trudeau dynasty (Pierre/Justin); Confederation 1867; largest coastline in world

current_leader.name: King Charles III
current_leader.title: Monarch (Head of State)
current_leader.notes: Represented by Governor General Mary Simon (first Indigenous GG, Inuk, since 2021)

prime_minister.name: Mark Carney
prime_minister.title: Prime Minister
prime_minister.notes: Liberal Party; former Bank of Canada/Bank of England governor; succeeded Trudeau; trade war with US; economic focus

former_leaders.name: Justin Trudeau
former_leaders.notes: Liberal; son of Pierre; legalized cannabis; carbon tax; SNC-Lavalin scandal; COVID response; Freedom Convoy 2022 (Emergencies Act); resigned amid party revolt

former_leaders.name: Stephen Harper
former_leaders.notes: Conservative; Alberta; economist; prorogation controversies; Senate scandal; tough-on-crime; residential school apology 2008

former_leaders.name: Paul Martin
former_leaders.notes: Liberal; finance minister who eliminated deficit; same-sex marriage legalized 2005; Gomery sponsorship scandal

former_leaders.name: Jean Chrétien
former_leaders.notes: Liberal; 'da little guy from Shawinigan'; 3 majorities; refused Iraq War; 1995 Quebec referendum (near-loss); Clarity Act

former_leaders.name: Brian Mulroney
former_leaders.notes: Progressive Conservative; Meech Lake/Charlottetown Accords (failed constitutional reforms); NAFTA/FTA; GST; PC party destroyed (2 seats 1993)

former_leaders.name: Pierre Elliott Trudeau
former_leaders.notes: Liberal; 'Trudeaumania'; Official Languages Act; War Measures Act 1970 (October Crisis); Charter of Rights 1982 (patriated Constitution); National Energy Program; bilingualism; 'Just watch me'; most influential modern PM

former_leaders.name: Lester B. Pearson
former_leaders.notes: Liberal; Nobel Peace Prize 1957 (Suez); medicare; Canadian flag; Auto Pact; bilingualism commission

former_leaders.name: John Diefenbaker
former_leaders.notes: Progressive Conservative; Bill of Rights; northern vision; Avro Arrow cancellation controversy

former_leaders.name: William Lyon Mackenzie King
former_leaders.notes: Liberal; longest-serving PM (22 years total); WWII leader; turned away Jewish refugees (MS St. Louis); spiritualist (seances); King-Byng Affair

910.name: First Peoples and Early Migration
910.description: Earliest human habitation of the Canadian landmass via Beringia and coastal routes, Paleo-Indian cultures, and Ice Age adaptation.

sub_clusters.name: Beringia and Coastal Migration Routes
sub_clusters.description: Human arrival via land bridge and Pacific coastal routes into present-day Yukon and British Columbia.

sub_clusters.name: Post-Glacial Adaptation
sub_clusters.description: Adaptation to retreating ice sheets, diversified subsistence strategies across emerging landscapes.

sub_clusters.name: Maritime Archaic Tradition
sub_clusters.description: Atlantic coast cultures in Labrador and Newfoundland, marine resource exploitation, burial mounds at L'Anse Amour.

910.name: First Nations Cultural Development
910.description: Diversification of Indigenous cultures across Canada: Woodland, Plains, Plateau, and Pacific Northwest traditions.

sub_clusters.name: Eastern Woodland Traditions
sub_clusters.description: Algonquian and Iroquoian peoples, horticulture, pottery, longhouse villages.

sub_clusters.name: Plains Buffalo Hunting Cultures
sub_clusters.description: Head-Smashed-In buffalo jump, communal hunting, Blackfoot and Cree peoples.

sub_clusters.name: Pacific Northwest Coast Cultures
sub_clusters.description: Haida, Tlingit, Kwakwaka'wakw, salmon economies, potlatch, monumental totem poles.

910.name: Inuit and Arctic Cultures
910.description: Pre-Dorset, Dorset, and Thule cultures of the Canadian Arctic and subarctic regions.

sub_clusters.name: Pre-Dorset Culture
sub_clusters.description: Early Paleo-Eskimo migration from Siberia, Arctic Small Tool tradition.

sub_clusters.name: Dorset Culture
sub_clusters.description: Artistic carvings, sea ice hunting, widespread Arctic habitation.

sub_clusters.name: Thule Culture and Expansion
sub_clusters.description: Whale-hunting ancestors of modern Inuit, eastward migration across Arctic Canada.

920.name: Norse Exploration and Vinland
920.description: Viking voyages to Newfoundland and Labrador, brief settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows.

sub_clusters.name: Leif Erikson and Vinland
sub_clusters.description: Norse discovery of Vinland, Markland, and Helluland in the sagas.

sub_clusters.name: L'Anse aux Meadows Settlement
sub_clusters.description: Only confirmed Norse settlement in the Americas, UNESCO World Heritage Site.

920.name: Haudenosaunee and Northern Iroquoian Confederacies
920.description: Formation and flourishing of the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois) and Wendat (Huron) confederacies straddling present-day Ontario and Québec.

sub_clusters.name: Great Law of Peace
sub_clusters.description: Constitutional founding of the Five Nations, consensus governance, wampum diplomacy.

sub_clusters.name: Wendat (Huron) Confederacy
sub_clusters.description: Georgian Bay confederacy, extensive trade networks, agricultural communities.

930.name: French Exploration and New France
930.description: From Cartier's voyages through the founding and expansion of New France, the fur trade, and missionary activity.

sub_clusters.name: Jacques Cartier's Voyages
sub_clusters.description: Three voyages exploring the St. Lawrence, claiming lands for France, contact with Stadacona and Hochelaga.

sub_clusters.name: Champlain and the Founding of Québec
sub_clusters.description: Samuel de Champlain founds Québec City (1608), explores the interior, forges Wendat alliance.

sub_clusters.name: Fur Trade and Coureurs des Bois
sub_clusters.description: Beaver pelt economy, coureurs des bois, voyageurs, Indigenous trade partnerships.

sub_clusters.name: Jesuit Missions in New France
sub_clusters.description: Jesuit missionaries among the Wendat and Algonquin, martyrdom of Brébeuf, mission communities.

930.name: British–French Rivalry and Conquest
930.description: Hudson's Bay Company founding, Anglo-French colonial wars, culminating in the British conquest of New France.

sub_clusters.name: Hudson's Bay Company
sub_clusters.description: Royal charter, fur trade monopoly, territorial control of Rupert's Land.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial Wars in North America
sub_clusters.description: King William's War, Queen Anne's War, King George's War — proxy conflicts of European rivalries.

sub_clusters.name: Seven Years' War in Canada
sub_clusters.description: French and Indian War, Battle of the Plains of Abraham (1759), fall of New France, Treaty of Paris.

sub_clusters.name: Acadian Expulsion (Le Grand Dérangement)
sub_clusters.description: Deportation of Acadians from Nova Scotia, diaspora to Louisiana and France.

940.name: British North America
940.description: Quebec Act, Loyalist migration, War of 1812, Rebellions of 1837-38, responsible government, and the path to Confederation.

sub_clusters.name: Quebec Act and Constitutional Acts
sub_clusters.description: Quebec Act (1774), Constitutional Act (1791), Upper and Lower Canada, Act of Union (1840).

sub_clusters.name: United Empire Loyalist Migration
sub_clusters.description: Tens of thousands of Loyalists resettle in Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, and Upper Canada after the American Revolution.

sub_clusters.name: War of 1812
sub_clusters.description: American invasion repelled, Tecumseh's alliance, Laura Secord, Battle of Queenston Heights, forging of Canadian identity.

sub_clusters.name: Rebellions of 1837–1838
sub_clusters.description: Papineau's Lower Canada rebellion and Mackenzie's Upper Canada revolt; crushed but led to Durham Report and responsible government.

940.name: Confederation and Dominion Building
940.description: Charlottetown and Québec conferences, British North America Act 1867, western expansion, and provincial creation.

sub_clusters.name: Confederation (1867)
sub_clusters.description: Fathers of Confederation, Charlottetown/Québec conferences, BNA Act creates Dominion of Canada.

sub_clusters.name: Red River Resistance and Louis Riel
sub_clusters.description: Métis resistance under Louis Riel, creation of Manitoba, execution of Thomas Scott.

sub_clusters.name: Canadian Pacific Railway
sub_clusters.description: National dream, Craigellachie last spike (1885), BC joins Confederation, Chinese railway workers.

sub_clusters.name: Northwest Rebellion (1885)
sub_clusters.description: Métis and First Nations uprising at Batoche, Riel's trial and execution, suppression of Indigenous resistance.

950.name: Canada in the World Wars
950.description: Canada's emergence as a nation through wartime sacrifice, from Vimy Ridge to Juno Beach.

sub_clusters.name: Canada in World War I
sub_clusters.description: Ypres, Somme, Vimy Ridge, Passchendaele; conscription crisis, Halifax Explosion.

sub_clusters.name: Interwar Canada
sub_clusters.description: Statute of Westminster (1931), Great Depression, Prairie dust bowl, Winnipeg General Strike.

sub_clusters.name: Canada in World War II
sub_clusters.description: Battle of the Atlantic, Dieppe Raid, D-Day (Juno Beach), liberation of the Netherlands, Japanese-Canadian internment.

950.name: Postwar and Modern Canada
950.description: Cold War, baby boom, immigration waves, Québec nationalism, and constitutional reform.

sub_clusters.name: Cold War and NATO
sub_clusters.description: NATO founding member, NORAD, Korean War, DEW Line, Avro Arrow cancellation, peacekeeping.

sub_clusters.name: Quiet Revolution
sub_clusters.description: Québec modernization, secularization, maîtres chez nous, Expo 67, FLQ October Crisis 1970.

sub_clusters.name: Pierre Trudeau and Patriation of Constitution
sub_clusters.description: Official bilingualism, multiculturalism policy, Charter of Rights and Freedoms (1982).

960.name: Québec Sovereignty Movement
960.description: Two referendums on Québec independence and the national unity crisis.

sub_clusters.name: 1980 Québec Referendum
sub_clusters.description: First sovereignty referendum, defeated 59.6% to 40.4%.

sub_clusters.name: Meech Lake and Charlottetown Accords
sub_clusters.description: Failed constitutional amendments, Elijah Harper's opposition, national frustration.

sub_clusters.name: 1995 Québec Referendum
sub_clusters.description: Razor-thin federalist victory, 50.58% to 49.42%, Clarity Act aftermath.

960.name: Indigenous Rights and Reconciliation
960.description: Oka Crisis, residential school reckoning, Truth and Reconciliation Commission, land claims, and MMIW.

sub_clusters.name: Oka Crisis
sub_clusters.description: Mohawk land dispute standoff near Montréal, armed confrontation, national awakening on Indigenous rights.

sub_clusters.name: Residential Schools and Truth & Reconciliation
sub_clusters.description: TRC (2008-2015), 94 Calls to Action, discovery of unmarked graves, national reckoning.

sub_clusters.name: Land Claims and Self-Government
sub_clusters.description: Nunavut creation (1999), modern treaties, Tsilhqot'in title decision (2014), UNDRIP adoption.

960.name: Contemporary Canada
960.description: Multiculturalism, NAFTA/CUSMA, climate action, COVID-19, and Canada's evolving global role.

sub_clusters.name: NAFTA, CUSMA, and Free Trade
sub_clusters.description: North American free trade, softwood lumber disputes, CUSMA renegotiation.

sub_clusters.name: Canada's Afghanistan Mission
sub_clusters.description: Kandahar deployment, combat role, 158 Canadian soldiers killed.

sub_clusters.name: COVID-19 in Canada
sub_clusters.description: Pandemic response, vaccine rollout, long-term care crisis, Freedom Convoy (2022).

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
